messages:
maria: Quick RFC follow-up — proposing a 'call shepherding' pattern for ingress. goal: attach a per-request timebudget that flows with the request and drives hedging, fallback and admission decisions. rough sketch below.
ajay: Sounds promising for SLO-aware hedging. question: how does this play with tenant rate limits and queued requests?
maria: Short answer: timebudget = min(client_deadline, ingress_allocated_window). ingress admission still uses token-bucket; if allocated_window is small we reject/queue. If final budget < min_hedge_threshold we mark the request as "fragile" and avoid spawning hedges but still allow fallbacks.
kevin: Big concern: streaming responses. if upstream is producing partial chunks slowly, how do we checkpoint the budget without killing useful progress? also KV cache implications for midstream hedges.
maria: Plan: checkpoint at logical framing boundaries — trailers or explicit progress events. If neither present, fallback to byte-heartbeats. Pseudocode: 
```
start = now()
while not done:
  time_left = budget - (now() - start)
  if time_left < hedge_threshold:
    cancel_pending_hedges()
  emit_trailer_if_done_or_progress("x-time-left", time_left_ms)
```
ops-bot: rollout checklist: feature flag `shepherding.enabled` in frontdoor config, default OFF for 2 weeks, telemetry opt-in. :white_check_mark:
lena: Observability reqs: we need token-level traces showing budget_at_ingress, hedges_spawned, hedge_outcome, final_outcome. add histogram metric `rw.timebudget_at_response_ms{route, outcome}`. also expose percentiles per-tenant.
david: Edge-case: client keeps connection open with slow throughput (tiny tokens every few seconds). we shouldn't abort when there is steady progress. maybe treat progress as a small budget refresh, but that could be gamed by clients.
ajay: Agreed. enforce refresh rules: progress events allowed at rate <= R per second and require monotonic cumulative progress. cap total refreshed time to, say, 30% of original budget or a fixed ceiling.
maria: Rollout/ops model: config enum per-tenant `timebudget_mode = {off, conservative, aggressive}`. conservative => hedges only when budget > 500ms; aggressive => hedges at >150ms. start all tenants with OFF, opt-in via feature flag for canaries. collect metrics 2 weeks then reconsider default.
kevin: Implementation notes: propagate a lightweight header `x-rw-timebudget-ms` for HTTP/gRPC and binary metadata for gRPC streams. keep it numeric and small. ensure proxies don't inflate headers on retries. also need change in tracer to carry that field and expose in span tags.
lena: Console work: add per-route view for timebudget SLI, hedging rate, hedge success rate, cost-per-request with hedges. I'll add a proto dashboard and mock data.
david: Billing: when hedges spawn we bill both primary+hedge; must annotate traces so Optimize can recommend policy changes to reduce cost. we should also expose a hedging-cost alert.
maria: I'll update the RFC with these clarifications and open a follow-up PR with: schema for `timebudget_mode`, frontdoor flag gating, header spec, unit tests for streaming checkpointing, and a small perf test harness. any objections to landing the draft today and iterating? @kevin
kevin: No objections. :thumbsup:
